questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go the US, I wanted to go somewhere warm and I wanted to go to a renowned University.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really enjoyed my stay, but it was a bit of a bummer that is was injured for my entire stay. Also I wish I would have stayed for two semesters rather than one.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some information by Email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Austin is very expensive and if want to pay a reasonable rent it can be pretty difficult.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Either you're going to pay a lot (1000-1300 dollars a month), or you will live further away from the school or in a co-op.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lived at 21 st co-op. By far the cheapest option, but in my opinion has some drawbacks. You have to labor, I had a roommate (you can have a private room though). Also generally the crowd wasn't really my cup of tea.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Registering for classes is a bit of a mess. As an exchange student you are last priority therefore a lot of classes a filled up. Furthermore some are locked by prerequisite requirements and department requirements. For example, I couldn't register for classes in the Athletic Training department as I was a Exercise Science major.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register online, after talking (or writing) with a guidance counselor.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The guidance counselor. She was very helpful to me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I would say pretty successful. Had to make some compromises, but was overall very satisfied with my classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To be relatively flexible. Also if a course is looked you can usually contact the professor directly and get a spot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were lower than the courses at University of Copenhagen. Might however be because of the classes I chose. Might have had a different experience if I had taken classes like Applied Physiology or Anatomy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Your grade is based upon point you get throughout the semester for assignments, exams etc. Also you have 3-4 exams per course, which really took me by surprise. So basically, you can't just cram all your studying into the last 2 weeks before the exam. Also a lot of memorization.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sport Psychology
Nutrition: Exercise/Health/Sport
Psychological Aspects of Exercise
Theory of Human Performance.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think Sport Psychology is an interesting course which isn't really being offered at KU (there is a course called Sport Psychology but has a different focus). Also really enjoyed Theory of Human Performance.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The insurance was crazy expensive. Also, I was caught a little off guard in regarding the price of housing in Austin.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Insurance and housing where more expensive than i expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have so many opportunities, especially if you're into sports and physical activity.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine..

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would have gone on a "adventure trip", if I weren't injured. Play some intramural sports. Also just hang out at clark field, there are often some people playing pick-up soccer, throwing frisbees, throwing footballs etc. Great way to meet people!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Check out the football games and other athletics.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, but I have been an exchange student in the US in High School previously.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with people in your classes. Do sports. Sign up for random stuff.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not sure.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The genrelal openess and energy of Americans.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do some sports.
Be open-minded.
Have some patience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know local people, and trying stuff I wouldn't normally back home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Understanding the social scene of college (clubs, organizations, greek life etc.)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
